nodes.title: Cracking Mobile Manipulation: From Failure Diagnosis to Agentic Robot System
nodes.authors: Zixuan Wang, Jia-Ning Li, Yinzhou Tang, Yanzhao Yu, Biao Wu, Meng Fang, Xin Li, Yiwu Zhong
nodes.summary: Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong performance on local robot manipulation, yet their success does not readily translate to long-horizon mobile manipulation. In our experiments, a pretrained subtask VLA achieves 80% success rate on atomic manipulation tasks but only 19% when these skills are composed into mobile manipulation. We argue that this gap stems from failures across the execution process rather than from local manipulation capability alone. To uncover these bottlenecks, we systematically diagnose failures in long-horizon mobile manipulation and identify three dominant regimes: task planning, navigation and base positioning, and local manipulation. Based on this diagnosis, we develop failure-guided agentic intervention that augments a fixed subtask VLA with demonstration-based planning guidance, adaptive visual memory, accessibility-aware base adjustment, and local end-effector adjustment. On RoboCasa365, these interventions progressively improve task success from 19% to 47%, with the finalized system reaching 49% on held-out episode seeds, compared with 18% for the baseline. The same design improves performance from 14% to 37% on BEHAVIOR-1K and from 5/20 to 13/20 on real-robot tasks. These results suggest that reliable mobile manipulation can be advanced by diagnosing and intervening on the current bottleneck, rather than uniformly scaling the underlying policy. Our code will be released at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/Cracking-Mobile-Manipulation.git.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: RoboSpan: Learning Modular Coordination Policies for High-DoF Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation with Teleoperation
nodes.authors: Keqiang Ren, Xuecheng Ye, Hanyu Liu, Zhihua Wang, Tao Jian, Yunsheng Ma, Jiayi Wen, Xinran Li, Zhigong Song
nodes.summary: Whole-body mobile manipulation suffers from two fundamental challenges: inherent motion heterogeneity across locomotion, arm, and hand modules, and progressive error accumulation over long-horizon multi-stage tasks. Existing teleoperation platforms also lack integrated dexterous tactile sensing to support coordinated whole-body decision-making. This paper presents RoboSpan, a high-DoF whole-body teleoperation and demonstration platform, and the Hierarchical Modular Framework (HMF) for learning modular coordination policies. HMF functionally decouples the 29-DoF action space into fine hand manipulation, arm pose adjustment, and mobile-base spatial configuration branches, and introduces the Coordinated Modular Embodied Transformer (COMET) with inter-modular cross-attention to enable dynamic information exchange and action coordination. Vision-language model driven hierarchical task decomposition structurally suppresses temporal error propagation, while a full-palm 2D tactile representation encodes distributed contact signals for cross-module tactile empowerment. Experiments on a physical 29-DoF robot demonstrate that the proposed method achieves over 20\% higher task success rate than mainstream baselines across a range of long-horizon whole-body tasks, markedly improving stability and robustness in contact-rich manipulation.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Back on Track: Deployment-time Policy Improvement via World Model Planning
nodes.authors: Colton Crosby, Hao Wang, Mac Schwager, Somil Bansal
nodes.summary: State-of-the-art visuomotor policies are increasingly capable of executing complex tasks, yet can fail during deployment in ways they cannot predict or recover from on their own. Improving their performance and robustness typically requires collecting more data, retraining, or modifying the policy architecture, all of which are time- and resource-intensive in practice. We instead propose an offline-trained monitoring-and-intervention framework that improves a policy during deployment using only black-box query access. From a limited set of labeled on-policy rollouts, we learn a policy-conditioned liveness value that measures the nominal policy's progress toward task completion; we additionally train a compact latent world model using these rollouts together with play data. At deployment, the liveness value continuously monitors execution. When it detects a loss of progress, a short-horizon planner searches the world model for corrective actions using the same value as its planning objective, after which control returns to the nominal policy. We evaluate our method on the LIBERO-Goal task suite and on a Franka Panda manipulator, using the vision-language-action model $π_{0.5}$ and a diffusion policy as nominal policies, and demonstrate significant improvements in task success rates, while supporting real-time control. Additional results and videos are available on the project website (https://policy-improvement-wm.pages.dev/).
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Dual-arm Cooperation for Tabletop Wiping with Temporal Object Removal
nodes.authors: Pengqi Zhang, Longchang Yu, Daohan Li, Liang Yan, Hangxin Liu
nodes.summary: We devise a dual-arm cooperative planning framework for wiping table surface in the presence of scattered objects. Unlike conventional surface-cleaning strategies that only cover free areas and detour around obstacles, our framework explicitly assigns one arm to rearrange objects while the other performs coverage wiping, thereby enabling access to previously obstructed regions. Specifically, we first construct a set of wiping and object-rearrangement action primitives. Based on these primitives, we introduce Geo-MILP, a geometry-aware task planner formulated as Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP). By integrating Logic-Based Benders Decomposition (LBBD), Geo-MILP iteratively optimizes action sequencingand timing to resolve geometric conflicts, promoting efficient cooperation between wiping and object rearrangement. We then employ K-Order Markov Optimization (KOMO) to generate smooth, collision-free motions to ensure feasible execution. Simulation and physical experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework not only increases reachable coverage by enabling access to obstructed areas, but also significantly improves time efficiency compared to Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) baselines, reducing planning time by up to 9 times and execution makespan by approximately 40%.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Dungeon and Visibility World Generator
nodes.authors: Edwin Mériaux, Antonio Loría, Gregory Dudek
nodes.summary: Robotic exploration, coverage, and multi-agent deployment algorithms require reproducible environments with controllable geometry and visibility. This paper presents the Dungeon and Visibility World Generator, an open-source framework for constructing two- and three-dimensional environments and evaluating geometric line-of-sight. The framework supports orthogonal, polygonal or polyhedral, and curvilinear geometries, with six construction families covering scattered rooms, clusters, winding passages, caverns, branches, and loops. Room dimensions, passage structures, obstacles, and spatial placement can be controlled through configurable parameters and probability distributions. Each generated environment provides continuous free-space geometry and a corresponding discrete occupancy representation. A Rust-based visibility engine supports line-of-sight queries in both representations, enabling the evaluation of observable regions from arbitrary agent positions. The framework records configurations, generated geometries, occupancy grids, and visibility results to support reproducible experiments. We demonstrate the generator across all six geometry classes, examine how geometry and spatial resolution affect visibility, and evaluate generation time and reproducibility. The resulting framework provides a configurable foundation for evaluating robotic exploration, coverage, and multi-agent deployment algorithms in diverse environments.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: HiFun: a Hierarchical Framework for Efficient Functional Dexterous Manipulation Learning
nodes.authors: Linyi Huang, Guowei Huai, Weibin Liu, Shulong Jiang, Ping Tan, Weixuan Zhang, Hui Zhang, Jie Song
nodes.summary: While multi-fingered dexterous robot hands have the potential to provide human-level dexterity, using them for functional manipulation remains difficult because task success depends on precise contact, coordinated arm-hand motion, and reactive recovery from execution errors. Precise contact depends on complex contact dynamics that are difficult to model accurately in simulation, motivating real-world learning. However, real-world demonstrations in the full arm-hand control space are costly and noisy because each trajectory must coordinate arm motion with high-DoF multi-finger contact. Small execution deviations can further cause slipped contact or premature force application, making recovery from off-nominal contact states important for robust execution. To deal with these challenges, we propose HiFun, a hierarchical real-world RL framework for functional dexterous manipulation tasks. Our key insight is to decouple the control complexity into a functional hand skill for precise contact execution and an arm-hand coordination policy for arm control and hand-skill activation. This design enables effective real-time human intervention for reactive recovery learning and efficient data collection with Dynamic Movement Primitive (DMP) augmentation. Across six real-world tasks on two dexterous hands, HiFun achieves 98.3% average success within one hour of online training and remains robust to dynamic disturbances. The project page is available at https://hly-123.github.io/HiFun/.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: VLRLA: Deployment-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models through In-Context Reinforcement Learning
nodes.authors: Diyuan Shi, Yiqi Tang, Hongyin Zhang, You Wu, Donglin Wang
nodes.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models connect visual perception and language understanding with robot control, providing a foundation for instruction-conditioned manipulation. However, conventional pretrained VLA policies lack a mechanism for gradual adaptation through accumulated interaction experience during deployment. We therefore propose VLRLA, a general framework that equips existing VLA models with \textit{in-context reinforcement learning} capabilities for deployment-time adaptation. Our approach augments a VLA model with a reinforcement learning module that learns from historical observations, actions, rewards, and termination signals. During deployment, the policy gradually refines its action generation and progressively improves task success while keeping model parameters fixed. Our approach is also designed for general applicability and compatibility with diverse learning history construction strategies and model training pipelines. Finally, through extensive experiments, we systematically investigate the learning properties of VLRLA in simulation and demonstrate its ability to adapt to unseen scenarios during real-world deployment.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Robota-Embed: Unified VLA Embeddings for Robot In-Context Learning and Evolution
nodes.authors: Yunze Liu, Jing Wang, Shenrui Wu, Wenkun He, Guanqi Zhan, Xianzheng Ma, Junyu Chen, Wenhang Ge, Haozhan Tang, Yuchao Gu, Zhuoyang Zhang, Zekai Wang, Dantong Niu, Zhen Dong, Yuke Zhu, Trevor Darrell, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Song Han, Han Cai
nodes.summary: Retrieving useful context for a robot requires matching its task, execution stage, and the continuation that should follow. We introduce Robota-Embed, to our knowledge the first vision-language-action (VLA) embedding model to jointly encode all three modalities in both current-state queries and recorded future continuations. Predictive retrieval training aligns these endpoints, enabling historical continuations to serve as context at inference time. We construct a multi-source corpus of 1,695,684 cleaned training anchors and introduce Robota-Embed-Bench, with 4,000 queries and a shared 8,000-entry gallery. Robota-Embed achieves 47.33% clip-level and 81.77% episode-level R@1, exceeding action-free Gemini Embedding 2 by 22.09 and 33.47 percentage points. Controlled retrieval studies show that removing native action degrades retrieval more than removing vision. We study two complementary applications. Embed2ICL uses retrieved experience for training-free and training-based policy conditioning, increasing success from 47.0% to 56.3% in DROID-Sim and from 86.4% to 92.8% on the LIBERO difficult subset, while improving task progress on real robots. Embed2Evolve uses execution feedback to grow task-local memory and refine context use around a frozen GPT-6 Astra policy. Across five ManiSkill tasks, it achieves 68% success, compared with 24% for GPT-6 Astra Direct and 33% for a harness independently evolved with Omni-Embed-Nemotron-3B under the same protocol. Relative to the latter, it uses approximately 79.5% fewer policy tokens per test rollout, counting both successes and failures. These results show that a unified, action-aware retrieval space can support robot in-context learning and task-local context evolution.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: IMU-Bench: Benchmarking Wrist IMU Representations Across Kinematic, Semantic and Clinical Tasks
nodes.authors: Yiquan Li, Aidan Bradshaw, Chenfeng Gao, Karan Ahuja
nodes.summary: Wrist-worn inertial measurement units (IMUs) provide a common sensing modality for tasks ranging from activity and gesture recognition to pose estimation, inertial odometry and clinical motor assessment. Existing wearable benchmarks evaluate performance across multiple tasks, but leave open how supervision for one task affects transfer to others and whether these tasks benefit from a shared representation. We present IMU-Bench, a benchmark of ten tasks from eight datasets for studying IMU multi-task performance and cross-task transfer. We compare six self-supervised methods pretrained on unlabeled recorded and simulated wrist motion, evaluating classification, pose and velocity estimation, and IMU-language retrieval. We find that our masked autoencoder, InrtlWrist, achieves the best or joint-best frozen-probe performance on nine of ten tasks, and fine-tuning improves on training from scratch on nine of ten tasks, including full-body pose, odometry and retrieval. Across transfer and joint-training experiments, supervision that benefits one target can reduce performance on others, with supervised sources transferring within kinematic estimation while, under frozen probing, none approaches the pretrained encoder on language retrieval, and joint-training gains that come at a cost to the paired task. These findings distinguish broad downstream usefulness from complementary task supervision. Code, task cards and a leaderboard are publicly available.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Active Generative Simulation: Meta-Learning What to Simulate for Sim-and-Real Policy Co-Training
nodes.authors: Liqian Ma, Vaibhav Saxena, Utkarsh Aashu Mishra, Shuo Cheng, Yongxin Chen, Danfei Xu
nodes.summary: Sim-and-real co-training is an effective way to scale robot learning by augmenting limited real-world demonstrations with simulation data. However, existing approaches typically treat simulators as fixed data sources, relying on uniform generation, offline retrieval, or manual parameter alignment by domain experts. We formulate \textit{Active Generative Simulation}: optimizing a simulator's data-generation distribution to maximize downstream real-world performance. To solve this problem, we propose MetaGenSim, a meta-learning framework that trains an auxiliary rater network via meta-gradients to automatically discover high-utility data-generation distributions within a user-specified simulation parameter space, without manual parameter alignment. Across simulation and real-world manipulation tasks, MetaGenSim outperforms uniform generation and retrieval baselines, achieves a 150% relative improvement in real-world full-task success over uniform generation, and matches expert manual alignment. We further show that distributions curated with a lightweight proxy policy transfer to VLA fine-tuning, and that MetaGenSim can exploit partial alignment through atomic skill stitching and object-receptacle composition when exact sim-and-real task alignment is unavailable. Project website: https://meta-gensim.github.io
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Spacecraft Pose Tracking via Kinematic Prediction and Selective Event Correction
nodes.authors: Yonglong Zhang, Guanning Yao, Shuo Zhang, Yifan Yang, Yang Liu†, Zongwu Xie
nodes.summary: In initialized spacecraft tracking, a short-horizon motion prediction remains available as event support changes. Observation-Aligned Event Innovation (OA-EI) uses events to correct selected components of this prediction. A constant-body-twist model propagates the complete pose; the event encoder proposes rotational and normalized image-plane translation corrections, retaining propagated axial depth. Candidate magnitudes come from a bounded Scale Gate and a deterministic activity factor, with empty windows returning the prediction unchanged. Evaluation uses four FRESH physical-event trajectories, twenty rollout starts, and three training seeds. Each rollout starts from two reference poses and then uses self-estimates. At 7.7 seconds, rotation and translation errors fall from 41.63°/57.28 mm for prediction alone to 15.73°/22.41 mm for OA-EI, reductions of 62.2% and 60.9%. Failure rates fall from 20.0% to 1.67%. Matched ablations favor the rotation-bearing interface for overall pose accuracy; combining scaling with activity support gives the lowest errors at every tested event-retention level. On Jetson Orin Nano, the measured in-memory update takes 44.56 milliseconds at the median and 58.77 milliseconds at P95.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Paraphrase Consensus Is Not Self-Consistency: Instruction Reliance and Robustness in VLA Policies
nodes.authors: Hanlong Li, Sihan Tan, Takeshi Ashizawa, Benjamin Yen, Kazuhiro Nakadai
nodes.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies fine-tuned on LIBERO are trained and evaluated on the same ten instruction strings, and rewording the instruction changes base OpenVLA's success by -38.0 points. Test-time prompt ensembling, which improves language models, does not recover this loss in any setting we ran. Paraphrase consensus (the medoid action over K paraphrases) costs base OpenVLA 16.8 points when the training instruction is a member. Without it, the medoid of the paraphrases scores -32.4 points relative to the training instruction, and confidence-based selection scores -28.0. The same medoid over samples of one paraphrase improves on greedy decoding but stays -27.6 points below the training instruction, consistent with aggregation reducing variance without removing the bias the paraphrases share. A wrong-instruction probe measures how much of a policy's success depends on the instruction. Across three policies and four suites, paraphrases cost a policy only where this share is high, and the stronger policies lose a much smaller fraction of it than base OpenVLA. LoRA post-training on paraphrased instructions reduces the one-paraphrase effect to +2.0 points, against -32.0 for a matched control, reproduces across two seeds and on OpenVLA-OFT, transfers to withheld phrasings, and leaves the policy's reliance on the instruction unchanged.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: $S^3$-Nav: Structured Spatial-Semantic Decision Making for Language-Guided Robot Navigation
nodes.authors: Chaemin Lee, Hae Min Cho
nodes.summary: This paper presents $S^3$-Nav, a structured spatial-semantic decision-making framework for language-guided robot navigation under partial observability. Rather than assuming a complete environment representation in advance, $S^3$-Nav incrementally constructs persistent spatial-semantic state while exposing only a capacity-controlled, task-conditioned view to the high-level policy. This separation decouples what the robot must retain from what the policy needs to inspect, allowing decision complexity to be controlled without discarding grounded evidence required for subsequent reasoning and validation. High-level navigation outputs remain provisional and are independently grounded and validated against persistent semantic evidence and current geometric observations before physical execution or task termination. Evaluations across multiple environments and object- and relation-goal tasks demonstrate that separating persistent state, decision-facing evidence, and execution authority improves closed-loop navigation reliability while reducing policy reasoning cost.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: From Failures to Learnable Worlds: Policy-Conditioned Environment Generation for Navigation Agents
nodes.authors: Yue Zhang, Han Lin, Zun Wang, Yidong Huang, Zaid Khan, Mohit Bansal
nodes.summary: Simulated environments enable scalable training data generation for embodied agents, but more data does not necessarily provide what a particular agent needs to learn. Existing environment-generation pipelines largely optimize generic properties such as realism, diversity, or task coverage, while different pretrained policies can fail for different environmental reasons. We therefore introduce WEDGE, a framework for weakness-guided navigation learning in which the failure modes of a pretrained agent guide the generation of training environments at each adaptation round. Given a pretrained policy, WEDGE uses an LLM to propose executable weakness features from contrasting successful and failed rollouts, automatically validates them on the diagnostic set, and selects the strongest validated weakness based on its success-rate gap. The validated weaknesses are then mapped to the environmental factors that control them. WEDGE varies these factors to construct environments in the difficulty regimes where the policy struggles, producing targeted training experience for adaptation. Across three navigation agents with different adaptation mechanisms, we find that policies exhibit distinct weakness profiles and benefit from different training environments. Weakness-conditioned adaptation consistently outperforms matched random and hard-example alternatives on ProcTHOR, while the resulting gains for Uni-NaVid and Gemini also extend to HM3D after ProcTHOR adaptation. Iterative re-diagnosis further shows that dominant weaknesses can persist or shift as the policy improves, providing updated guidance for subsequent environment construction. Together, these results show that policy failures are not only diagnostic signals, but actionable guidance for constructing training environments that target a policy's current weaknesses.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: A VR Training System for Robot-Assisted Vascular Intervention with Dual-Mode Control and Model-Based Interaction Response
nodes.authors: Yining Shang, Shuxiang Guo, Sheng Cao, Pengcheng Li, Bin Wang, Mingchao Ding
nodes.summary: Virtual reality training for robot-assisted vascular intervention requires accurate robotic control and effective feedback on guidewire--vessel interactions. This paper presents a VR training system combining asynchronous dual-mode command mapping with sensorless interaction estimation. The system supports velocity-controlled navigation and position-driven incremental manipulation. Guidewire deformation and a Hunt--Crossley-type contact response are combined and temporally filtered to estimate interaction intensity, while trajectory-based visualization supports post-procedure review. Tests confirmed distinct command-dispatch patterns across three velocity gears and the position mode. During hybrid-scene navigation, the estimated response remained low during straight insertion and increased as the guidewire bent within the vascular model. Trajectory analysis yielded a model-derived cumulative trauma work (CTW) value of 15.166 in normalized units and localized regions of elevated interaction. In a preliminary study with 15 novices, physical-phantom task success increased from 53.3% to 93.3% after VR training, while mean completion time decreased from 132.4 s to 96.7 s. These results demonstrate the system's dual-mode operation, deformation-sensitive feedback, and potential to improve subsequent physical-phantom task performance.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Topology-Preserving Multi-Usage Pipe Centerline Refinement under Permanent Tubular Occupancy
nodes.authors: Deng Quan
nodes.summary:
Discrete multi-group pipe routers place channels on a grid or coarse graph. The resulting centerlines are topologically feasible but typically contain many axis-aligned corners. For permanently occupied fluid tubes---as in additively manufactured hydraulic manifolds---those corners are undesirable: they degrade geometric fairness and, in practice, flow quality. This technical report studies the downstream geometric stage that starts from a fixed routing topology and a feasible coarse layout, and refines tubular centerlines under permanent clearance.
  Unlike classical robotic path smoothing, which usually fair one temporary open trajectory, our setting is a branched manifold with declared terminal usages, finite tube radii, and static cross-group occupancy. We formalize the refinement problem, highlight the multi-usage junction conflict that a single shared branch point cannot resolve, and outline a hybrid trunk-share / junction-split parameterization with soft geometric costs and hard clearance acceptance. On a multi-group suite ($8$ groups $\times$ $8$ terminals, $r{=}2$) with capsule clearance, the refine reaches full hard-accept success, $κr\lesssim 1$, and about a $95\%$ relative drop in the soft objective. Physics-based pressure-drop optimization is intentionally deferred to a later PDE stage; here the objective remains geometric.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: A Master-to-Simulation Interface with Demonstration-Trajectory Guidance for Vascular Intervention
nodes.authors: Mingyu Zou, Shuxiang Guo, Sheng Cao, Pengcheng Li, Jian Guo, Bin Wang, Mingchao Din
nodes.summary: Robotic vascular intervention can reduce radiation exposure to physicians and improve manipulation stability, but effective guidance remains challenging because conventional fluoroscopic images provide limited spatial information. This paper developed a vascular intervention interactive system that connects a real robotic master controller with the SOFA(Simulation Open Framework Architecture) physical simulation platform and reused successful operation trajectories as visual guidance in physical phantom experiments. Experiments were conducted to validate the master-to-SOFA control loop and to compare three guidance conditions: no guidance, centerline guidance, and successful-trajectory guidance. The control validation results showed reliable command delivery under velocity-mode operation. In the physical phantom experiment, centerline guidance showed no obvious improvement over no guidance. In contrast, successful trajectory guidance provided a clear performance benefit. Compared with the no-guidance condition, it reduced task completion time, collision number, rollback number, and rotation number by approximately 66.8%, 34.3%, 55.6%, and 66.7%, respectively. These results indicate that successful trajectories obtained under instrument-vessel interaction can provide practical guidance cues, offering a simple and effective visual assistance strategy for robotic vascular intervention experiments.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Beyond Kinematic Tracking: Preserving Expressive Characteristics in Humanoid Whole-Body Control
nodes.authors: Lingfan Bao, Hanshang Zhu, Yan Pan, Jincheng Wang, Jingyang Yu, Tianhu Peng, Yiyang Jia, Dimitrios Kanoulas, Chengxu Zhou
nodes.summary: Whole-body control plays a crucial role in enabling humanoid robots to execute expressive motions. Faithful execution requires preserving both the intended action and its expressive characteristics. Existing whole-body trackers typically balance joint and keypoint tracking with physical stability across diverse motions, but these objectives do not necessarily prioritize the expressive characteristics of each action. Our analysis shows that lower average positional tracking error does not guarantee better preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics. To address this gap, we propose a residual learning framework with compensation objectives targeting amplitude, energy, body expansion, body lean, and pelvis height. To concentrate compensation while limiting interference with the underlying tracking behavior, motion-aware gating allocates correction capacity according to body-part activity, preserving larger correction ranges in more active parts and restricting them elsewhere. For each frozen tracker, we train motion-specific residual policies and distill them into a unified policy shared across motion categories. Simulation and physical experiments on the Unitree G1 across eight motion categories demonstrate superior preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics compared with the corresponding baselines.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
nodes.authors: Minghao Guo, Qingyue Jiao, Xiujin Liu, Jianhong Pang, Ruimeng Yang, Naihao Xu, Liwei Che, Haochen Xue, Ziqi Wang, Xinying Cai, Jiaxuan Luo, Jiaxin Deng, Xuesong Ye, Jintao Qu, Wenyao Gao, Jingwen Gu, Chenyang Zhao, Shichun Liu, Guibin Zhang, Zefang Liu, Siyin Wang, Wujiang Xu, Danrui Li, Zeru Shi, Woongyeong Yeo, Shuang Liu, Wei-Chieh Huang, Weizhi Zhang, Tianyu Yang, Kangsan Kim, Yebowen Hu, Bowen Wen, Bowen Jiang, Haohao Su, Ming Yin, Sheldon Yu, Mian Zhang, Yuyan Chen, Hanrong Zhang, Kai Mei, Zihao Zhang, Mingyu Jin, Xi Zhu, Hengyi Wang, Tianxin Wei, Linyong Nan, Zhenwen Liang, Zhendong Chu, Ziqi Huang, Yongye Su, Sixun Dong, Shujian Liu, Kaiqu Liang, Jiaojiao Han, Zhaoye Fei, Kun Wang, Shihan Dou, Zhichun Guo, Xingjian Diao, Zeqi Gu, Heng Wang, Tao Feng, Cheng Qian, Hamid Palangi, Silei Xu, Xi Yun, Yi Zhu, Shilong Liu, Qingsong Wen, Sung Ju Hwang, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang, Yiyu Shi, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Jiaxuan You, Julian McAuley, Mengdi Wang, Jiawei Han, Philip S. Yu, Ziyi Ye
nodes.summary: Multimodal models and agents have emerged to enable AI systems to learn from and interact with the real world more like humans by integrating information across multiple modalities. However, enabling multimodal agents to continually acquire useful information from complex, heterogeneous multimodal data remains a significant challenge as they move toward long-horizon tasks and lifelong settings. Addressing this challenge requires effective memory mechanisms that can maintain continuity across sessions, adapt to changing users and environments, and refine memory-management policies through accumulated experience. We introduce a two-axis analytical framework for multimodal agent memory structured around two key questions: how multimodal information is formed and represented (Axis I, Formation and Representation), and how its management adapts with accumulated experience (Axis II, Memory Management). Axis I, Formation and Representation, characterizes what information is retained and how it is encoded (e.g., modality-specific embeddings, textual and structured records, latent and parametric representations) to support subsequent reasoning and action. Axis II, Memory Management, distinguishes three tiers: T1 Static Memory reuses fixed memory; T2 Dynamic Memory updates memory through a stable policy; and T3 Self-Evolving Memory updates memory through an evolving policy. Based on this framework, we synthesize recurring design patterns and derive principles for balancing source fidelity with abstraction, maintaining temporal validity and provenance, grounding memory use in recoverable evidence, and evolving memory policies over time. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and potential future directions for the memory mechanism of multimodal agents.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: VLX-Go: Robust Embodied Tracking through Multi-Stage Learning and On-Policy Refinement
nodes.authors: Kyusong Lee, Heting Ying, Tiancheng Zhao
nodes.summary: Embodied visual tracking requires a robot to identify a designated target from visual observations and control its own motion to follow that target through an environment. Following an isolated person is a comparatively simple demonstration of embodied visual tracking, but following the intended person among distractors remains challenging. Existing methods exhibit a substantial drop in success from single-target to distractor tracking, motivating a focus on the shared spaces that person-following robots must navigate. We present \method{}, a vision--language waypoint policy built around the hypothesis that visual and language representations should be aligned before tracking-specific motion is learned. The policy combines complementary frozen visual encoders, multiscale temporal context, a transformer backbone, and a lightweight head for robot-centric waypoint prediction. Its training progresses through vision--language alignment, multimodal reasoning mid-training, and tracking specialization on 19,532 oracle episodes. Compared with 41.54\% distractor-tracking success for our earlier OmTrackVLA model, the complete multi-stage recipe achieves 55.80\%. We then explore on-policy refinement using filtered oracle labels for states visited by the policy. This preliminary study adds 2.42 percentage points of distractor-tracking success, reaching 58.22\%, while reducing collision rate by 1.99 pts. The final policy records the highest distractor- and ambiguous-tracking success rates among the compared methods. These results support staged multimodal learning as a promising direction for tracking among distractors and motivate further study of on-policy refinement for person following in shared spaces.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Probabilistic Physics Digital Twin for Human-Robot Interaction
nodes.authors: Yushen Hu, Harshvardhan Chandirasekar, Apurv Kushwaha, Jonathan King, Zhu-Tian Chen
nodes.summary: Digital twins are increasingly used in robotics to simulate interactions, predict action outcomes, and support planning. However, constructing accurate digital twins requires precise estimates of physical properties such as mass, friction, and center of mass, which are often difficult to obtain in real-world environments. We propose probabilistic digital twins, which represent uncertain physical properties as probability distributions rather than fixed values. By simulating actions across these distributions, the twin predicts a range of possible outcomes and their likelihoods. These probabilistic simulations can guide both human and robot actions by identifying actions that are effective despite physical uncertainty. We demonstrate this framework through human-robot interaction scenarios, including interfaces that communicate simulated outcomes to users and robot planning strategies that explicitly account for uncertainty.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: NavAble: A Large-Scale Dataset and Synthetic Data Generation Pipeline for Blind Navigation
nodes.authors: Hochul Hwang, Jahir Sadik Monon, Soowan Yang, Shiven Umeshbhai Patel, Anh Nhat Hong Nguyen, Kien Nguyen, Keshav Garg, Dylan Gage, Duretti Hordofaa, Anshu Anjna, Eshed Ohn-Bar, Donghyun Kim
nodes.summary: Reliable recognition of accessibility-critical objects (e.g., audible pedestrian signals, door-activation buttons, and handrails) is essential for assistive navigation technologies that support safe, independent mobility for blind and low-vision (BLV) users. Yet these categories are underrepresented in existing large-scale vision datasets, and the few datasets that include them suffer from limited class coverage, inconsistent annotations, and poor diversity. We introduce NavAble, a large-scale dataset spanning 11 accessibility-critical object classes, combining 41K curated open-source images with 8K newly collected, densely annotated real-world images. To extend scale and diversity, we develop a synthetic data generation pipeline that renders high-fidelity 3D assets across 37 environments under diverse styles and viewpoints, yielding 452K frames with rich ground-truth annotations from 565 assets. The pipeline minimizes manual effort by combining automated web image crawling, VLM-based filtering, SAM 3D-based asset generation, and convenient camera trajectory configuration, enabling large-scale data generation at a diversity unattainable through manual collection. Experiments show that fine-tuning existing segmentation models on the NavAble Dataset achieves reliable accessibility-object segmentation (>80% mIoU on our held-out test set). We also demonstrate the effectiveness of synthetic data augmentation, which yields up to +3.5 mIoU over real-world-only fine-tuning. Beyond benchmark evaluation, validation on egocentric data from two mobility-assistive robots demonstrates improved perception reliability in real-world navigation scenarios. Together, NavAble establishes a scalable foundation for BLV navigation perception, directly addressing the data scarcity and embodiment gaps. The dataset and pipeline are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/NavAble/NeurIPS_2026_BLV.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: DeSpatial: The devil of Agentic Spatial Reasoning Lies in 3D Itself
nodes.authors: Yifei Liu, Xiaolong Zhou, Ziyang Gong, Yifan Zhou, Yuanyuan Gao, Yuning Gong, Yuchen Yang, Hongjie Zhang, Xue Yang, Xiao Sun, Zhihang Zhong
nodes.summary: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. A simple oracle experiment exposes this perception bottleneck: replacing tool-predicted perception with ground-truth 3D bounding boxes raises an agent to nearly full score across five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, while retaining the same reasoning tools. Motivated by this finding, we believe the devil of spatial reasoning lies in 3D itself, and introduce DeSpatial(Devil of Spatial), which explicitly decomposes spatial understanding into perception and reasoning. DeSpatial has a shared 3D perception tool to reconcile independent perception outputs into a unified, metric, gravity-aligned 3D scene. This perception tool has two core components: a) a joint segmentation--depth co-refinement module that consolidates masks of the same object and removes projection artifacts caused by inconsistent segmentation and depth within a single frame; b) a cross-view instance fusion module that consolidate voxel-overlapping instances but not allowed to merge same-frame instances. This fusion module additionally fuses spatially disjoint fragments caused by insufficient multi-view observations, by checking their 3D structure and source mask appearance. After receiving the complete and unified 3D scene information, the agent chooses reasoning or computational tools to solve the spatial problem. DeSpatial achieves leading performance on VSI-Bench, MindCube-Tiny, and ViewSpatial, with additional long-video results on VSI-SUPER, revealing the bottleneck of spatial understanding lies in a precise 3D perception itself.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: PiCo: Physics-Informed Concept Probing for Geo-Foundation Models
nodes.authors: Yihang She, Andrew Blake, Jianbo Qi, Srinivasan Keshav
nodes.summary: Geo-foundation models (GFMs) are typically evaluated by downstream task predictive performance, revealing little about which physical features they are sensitive to or use in prediction. This limits developers' ability to test hypotheses about model behaviour and users' ability to select models for new tasks. We propose Physics-Informed Concept Probing (PiCo), a post-hoc framework for explaining GFM predictions. PiCo identifies concept vectors in a GFM's embedding space by generating synthetic multispectral satellite observations from a 3D radiative transfer model coupled with a game engine. These vectors reveal physical sensitivities that inform domain-based hypotheses about downstream performance. Projecting embeddings onto these concept vectors produces low-dimensional representations for quantifying concept importance in making predictions. We evaluate PiCo on three GFMs with different input modalities using seven physical concepts covering forest leaf optics and canopy structure. In ground-cover estimation, RGB restriction reduces dry-matter sensitivity and disproportionately degrades predictions for dry vegetation and bare ground, supporting a hypothesis derived from sensitivity analysis. For hierarchical forest type and tree species classification, concept representations retain 70.0-93.8% of full-embedding accuracy. Models capture similar physical contrasts between classes, such as structural differences between broadleaf forest and cleared ground and leaf-water-content differences between oak and beech, yet differ in the strength of these contrasts and the concepts driving classification. PiCo thus provides a physical basis for hypothesis testing and model assessment, with potential applicability beyond Earth observation wherever forward models enable controlled simulation and pretrained embeddings are accessible for probing.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: Intern Lumina U2: A Multi-Codebook Diffusion Large Language Model for Omni-Visual Understanding and Image Generation
nodes.authors: Qian Yu, Zongyang Qiu, Juncheng Yan, Hongliang Li, Qi Qin, Keqi Wang, Siqi Luo, Junkui Ju, Yapeng Mi, Tiantian Lu, Tian Liu, Pengyu Xie, Chenhao Ji, Minghui Zhang, Yiang Zhao, Siyu Yan, Haiying Xu, Yanbo Wang, Jianghan Shen, Yuandong Pu, Jiayi Lei, Borui Zhang, Jinxin Shi, Bo Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Shenglong Ye, Lixin Gu, Hongjie Zhang, Linghan Liu, Xinyuan Chen, Yuewen Cao, Lihe Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Junjun He, Qiangwei Liu, Qi Zhang, Yu Cheng, Tianfan Xue, Hui Xiong, Chang Xu, Yu Qiao, Yihao Liu, Bin Fu
nodes.summary: Unified multimodal generation covers discrete, continuous, and hybrid paradigms. Discrete approaches with single-codebook visual tokenizers align naturally with text modeling but have limited representational capacity. Continuous and hybrid approaches retain richer visual representations, but they model text and images in heterogeneous spaces with different training objectives, potentially introducing optimization conflicts between modalities with misaligned representation spaces. These choices expose a central question: how to efficiently model high-capacity visual representations alongside textual content in a shared optimization space within a single backbone. We present Intern Lumina U2, to our knowledge the first diffusion language model to represent multi-codebook visual tokens in a fully discrete space. Each visual position is represented by a group of codes from complementary codebooks, increasing its representational capacity while preserving compatibility with discrete text modeling. At the input, the embeddings are concatenated at each position; at the output, a lightweight multi-codebook autoregressive head predicts the codes within each position sequentially, while the diffusion backbone processes all positions in parallel. Built on the unified 4D representation of AToken, Intern Lumina U2 supports image, video, and 3D inputs within a single backbone and achieves leading performance among unified models in visual understanding, image generation, and image editing. We further build a full-stack training, inference, and evaluation system on both Ascend and NVIDIA platforms to verify the cross-platform effectiveness of our model. We also improve the inference efficiency through a stability-aware sampling strategy, which combines confidence-plateau-guided unmasking approach with drift-triggered cache refreshing mechanisms, accelerating image generation by 4.45x.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: ReasonUni: Reasoning-Augmented Reconstruction Advances Unified Multimodal Models
nodes.authors: Feize Wu, Zhiyuan Yan, Yuhuan Hong, Yuwei Niu, Zongjian Li, Zheyuan Liu, Bin Lin, Jinbo Yan, Jie Qin, Xudong Mao, Limeng Qiao, Guanglu Wan, Li Yuan
nodes.summary: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. We propose ReasonUni, a reasoning-augmented reconstructive post-training framework that extends this coupling beyond perception. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. To jointly optimize both modules, we introduce TreeGRPO, a tree-structured reinforcement learning method that samples multiple reasoning paths and candidate images per path, then aggregates visual rewards to update both modules under a unified objective. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains in both understanding and generation, showing that reasoning-augmented reconstruction yields genuine mutual gains for UMMs.

nodes.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
nodes.authors: Jahyeok Koo, Hyeonseo Yu, Seungho Jang, Jaewoo Jung, Jiwon Kang, Seokju Cho, Seungryong Kim
nodes.summary: Generating novel views from limited observations requires preserving both the appearance and spatial structure of a scene. Although recent approaches exploit fine-grained geometric cues, they do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes, and inter-object relationships. In this work, we investigate whether 3D language understanding can provide complementary supervision for novel-view generation. We introduce Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. Our model incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations and leverages understanding features during generation through joint self-attention with a modality-aware attention masking strategy. Experiments demonstrate strong image quality and geometric consistency in novel-view generation, alongside competitive 3D language understanding. Further analysis shows that joint training improves cross-view correspondence in VAE representations and similarity in a 3D-aware feature space.

nodes.title: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
nodes.authors: Dongyue Lu, Guian Fang, Hur Lim, Yonggang Wu, Yanrong Wang, Hongshan Chen, Shengju Qian, Yue Liao, Wei Chow, Lingdong Kong, Tianxin Huang, Yu Yang, Hongji Yang, Junchao Huang, Ao Liang, Yihao Wang, Zihan Wang, Rong Li, Hanlin Chen, Xin Wang, Wei Tsang Ooi, Mike Zheng Shou, Shuicheng Yan
nodes.summary: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. For input preservation, registered RGB-D references and annotated anchors support appearance, geometry, and spatial stability measurements. For generated-content persistence, we compare revisits to regions absent from the input image with their first generated observations to test whether models preserve what they create. For 3D self-consistency, cross-view depth and feature correspondence, regional scale agreement, and held-out Gaussian rendering test whether generated views describe the same 3D scene. Minute-long exploration and revisits further test long-term consistency. Our construction and annotation pipeline brings together public datasets, self-captured scenes, and simulation, yielding 720 instances across indoor and outdoor environments and six exploration-and-revisit protocols. Evaluation spans 27 text-, action-, and camera-conditioned models through native-interface adapters. Our Orbia benchmark provides a systematic basis for diagnosing 3D inconsistency and developing more persistent video world models.

nodes.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
nodes.authors: Ao Liang, Youquan Liu, Mingxiao Li, Wei Chow, Lingdong Kong, Yue Liao, Dongyue Lu, Yu Yang, Wei Yin, Runnan Chen
nodes.summary: World-action models aim to turn visual anticipation into driving decisions, yet typically train action experts on trajectory representations defined independently of visual dynamics. This motivates deriving action targets directly from visual motion. We first examine a simpler setting in which trajectories are reconstructed from recorded future images. Even without the need for future prediction, reconstruction captures the dominant maneuver but leaves centimeter-scale errors. We therefore introduce VITAL (Vision-Induced Tokens for Action Learning), an action tokenizer that couples a visually derived motion scaffold with a compact residual encoding the trajectory error left by that scaffold. This representation makes visual motion the principal prediction target and gives small metric corrections a separate, normalized learning scale. Using flow matching, the action expert jointly predicts both components from the current image, ego state, and navigation command, without generating future images at inference. The same residual coordinates support bounded reinforcement post-training that refines execution while keeping the predicted visual scaffold fixed. With only one action denoising step, VITAL achieves 90.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, within 0.13 points of its ten-step score at 3.29x the end-to-end inference speed. Without retraining, it achieves 91.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest and 38.6 on navhard. Project page: https://worldbench.github.io/vital

nodes.title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
nodes.authors: Qihang Cao, Haoyuan Li, Zihan Guo, Sensen Gao, Zihui Gao, Huixin Zhang, Fan He, Jianhua Han, Hang Xu, Xiaodan Liang, Jia-Wang Bian
nodes.summary: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. Our analysis reveals that this spatial--dynamic interference is highly non-uniform across parameter groups, with the balance between static and dynamic capabilities particularly sensitive to changes in late-layer MLPs. To address this interference, we propose DynThinker, a unified framework for jointly strengthening static and dynamic spatial reasoning. Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters while preserving flexibility for capability enhancement. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) complements D-EMA by selectively integrating spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance. Across ten metrics spanning nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, DynThinker achieves the highest average score among all evaluated models. Notably, DynThinker achieves 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under the sample-wise and group-wise evaluation protocols of DSI-Bench, respectively, setting new state-of-the-art results among the compared open-source models across all four evaluations within a unified model.

nodes.title: GeoThinker-$F$: Endogenous Predictive World Representations for Fast Spatial Intelligence
nodes.authors: Haoyuan Li, Qihang Cao, Huanyuan Zhou, Xin Hu, Sijia Chen, Zihan Guo, Kun Xiang, Yunshuang Nie, Tao Tang, Xinlong Zheng, Jia-Wang Bian, Xianming Liu, Xiaodan Liang
nodes.summary: Existing geometry-aware Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on external 3D encoders to provide structural priors, but executing these additional encoder paths at inference introduces substantial latency and computational overhead. We propose GeoThinker-$F$, an efficient framework that internalizes spatiotemporal perception by transforming causal MLLM hidden states into predictive latent world representations. Our key insight is that intermediate semantic representations contain sufficient information to predict useful representations of current geometry and future semantics, without requiring an exact reproduction of features from a dedicated 3D encoder. To realize this idea, GeoThinker-$F$ adopts a decoupled two-stage training strategy. In the first stage, the MLLM backbone is frozen while lightweight Latent Frame Prediction (LFP) heads learn from an offline 3D geometry expert and next-frame semantic targets. In the second stage, the external expert is removed, and the model is jointly optimized to generate and selectively integrate its self-predicted priors through a specialized Spatial-Grounded Temporal (SGT) Fusion module. Extensive evaluations show that GeoThinker-$F$ eliminates runtime dependence on external 3D geometry encoders while maintaining competitive performance across diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks. It achieves up to a $3.6\times$ inference speedup, reducing latency from $1.45\,\mathrm{s}$ to $0.40\,\mathrm{s}$ while retaining strong spatial reasoning performance.

nodes.title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
nodes.authors: Seungmi Choi, Ji-Hyoun Choi, Suhyun Jo, Tae-Gwon Park, Hui Yong Kim
nodes.summary: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods enable efficient reconstruction of 3D scenes from sparse multi-view images in a single forward pass, without scene-specific optimization. However, existing feed-forward scene-coding pipelines first generate a complete Gaussian representation and then encode its geometry and appearance attributes separately, often involving non-differentiable operations. The resulting 'generate-then-compress' pipeline requires complex attribute-specific codec designs and limits rate-distortion performance by restricting the exploitation of cross-attribute redundancy. We propose multi-view feature coding for Gaussian splatting (MFGS), an end-to-end feed-forward framework for scene coding. Instead of compressing an explicit Gaussian representation, MFGS extracts multi-view features from the input images and encodes them into a compact bitstream. Through end-to-end rate-distortion training, MFGS learns compact multi-view features that jointly represent geometry and appearance, enabling the receiver to predict Gaussian attributes from the decoded features. We further introduce importance-guided Gaussian selection to accommodate different rendering budgets, allowing the receiver to adjust the number of Gaussians used for rendering from the same bitstream. Across RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, MFGS achieves 99.76-99.86% bitrate savings over the generate-then-compress pipeline, as measured by BD-rate, while reducing total GMACs by 52-55% and providing an approximately 12 times end-to-end speedup.

nodes.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
nodes.authors: Mingyu Ouyang, Yiran Wang, Siyuan Hu, Xingyilang Yin, Huiqiang Sun, Guangzhi Wang, Junfu Pu, Cheng Cheng, Honghao Chen, Ying Shan, Mike Zheng Shou, Hwee Tou Ng
nodes.summary: Computer-use agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions. However, games, with their visually rich worlds and diverse mechanics, remain challenging and offer a demanding next step toward general digital control. Current game-agent learning pipelines often rely on large-scale demonstrations with limited coverage of dynamic game states, while scalable environments for interactive training remain difficult to obtain. We introduce Player-1, a post-training framework for learning game control beyond demonstrations through synthetic experience. We extend the computer-use action space with relative pointer motion, sustained inputs, and composite actions. For supervised initialization, we fine-tune computer-use models on 6,044 curated gameplay trajectories that pair recorded actions with task instructions and visual reasoning. We construct Player-1-Gym, sixteen synthetic 2D and 3D environments designed around control demands shared across games. Programmatically verifiable rewards and randomized observations and control dynamics support multi-environment reinforcement learning with PPO. The resulting Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B improve MineDojo-300 success over their SFT policies by 27.8 and 17.7 percentage points, respectively. Player-1-9B reaches 38.33% success compared with 12.63% for the strongest evaluated baseline, with further gains over SFT on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld. Further analyses show that broader synthetic environment coverage improves transfer, while the use of composite actions that combine multiple keyboard and mouse inputs increases during RL. We demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience substantially improves game control beyond supervised initialization, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.

nodes.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
nodes.authors: Weijie Wang, Haomin Zhang, Ye Li, Akide Liu, Zeyu Zhang, Haoyu Zhao, Yefei He, Donny Y. Chen, Feng Chen, Bohan Zhuang
nodes.summary: Long-form agentic video generation must turn a screenplay into shots that remain spatially and temporally consistent across nonconsecutive requests. Passing prompts or recent frames between shots does not provide a shared spatial frame for revisiting a scene or a time-indexed record for replaying an earlier event. We present Any Time, Any Space (ATAS), which compiles a screenplay into shot requests with explicit location, camera, and event-time references. Before generation, it retrieves relevant evidence from a scene memory of registered static geometry and an event memory of dynamic observations indexed by scene, event, and time. After generation, ATAS reconstructs and registers the clip. It updates memory only when review and state checks accept the observation, while film delivery remains independent of memory admission. Across four video generators, ATAS improves all reported cross-shot consistency measures and achieves the highest aggregate benchmark score for each backbone. It also outperforms the compared agents and 3D-guided methods on target-image spatial revisit, leads three event-recapture criteria, and receives the highest human ratings on all six criteria. The video results and code are available on our project page: https://lhmd.top/atas/.

nodes.title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
nodes.authors: Weichen Lyu, Chong Xia, Mingyu Dong, Long Xu, Shengjun Zhang, Yueqi Duan
nodes.summary: 3D object composition is pivotal to digital content creation and robot simulation, while also serving as a critical testbed for physical intelligence in foundation models. Previous methods either leverage large language models to directly predict object coordinates, or utilize generative diffusion priors to synthesize composite images for visual alignment, both of which rely on static priors in digital spaces. However, these methods consistently struggle with complex compositions such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling and hidden containment, as these tasks require interactive construction processes involving global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation. To address these challenges, we propose PhySGA, a Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for 3D composition via agent exploration and physical simulation, enabling the universal interactive assembly of rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Directly applying vanilla LLMs or VLMs to this task proves insufficient, as current models inherently lack grounded physical understanding and interactive construction experience. To overcome this limitation, we design a collaborative feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent focuses on geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, while a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics for simulator state diagnosis and fine-grained closed-loop correction. Furthermore, Action Routers map semantic planning and analysis onto executable physical primitives within the simulator, while a task-specific Self-Evolving Skill Library distills historical trial-and-error feedback into reusable experiences, boosting success rates and minimizing exploration attempts. Extensive experiments within Isaac Sim demonstrate that PhySGA significantly surpasses existing methods in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.

nodes.title: VascuSR: Iterative Anatomy-Aware Diffusion for CT Super-Resolution
nodes.authors: Hairong Ni, Jiahe Huang, Minghao Guo, Wojciech Matusik, Rose Yu
nodes.summary: Generative super-resolution (SR) can recover sharp detail in computed tomography (CT) images from severely downsampled observations, but the missing high-frequency content is not uniquely determined by the low-resolution input. Consequently, visually plausible reconstructions may contain anatomically unsupported vascular detail, such as missing, spurious, or incorrectly connected vessels. To overcome this challenge, we introduce VascuSR, an iterative anatomy-aware diffusion framework that combines image reconstruction with explicit 3D vascular guidance. First, to provide richer anatomical guidance, we use an explicit 3D vascular representation that captures structural information beyond individual slices. This representation also simplifies vascular refinement by allowing a lightweight 3D generative refiner to focus on vascular structure rather than complex CT appearance. Second, to guide slice-wise SR, a lightweight anatomy controller injects the refined structure into the diffusion decoder, while iterative feedback updates this guidance from each new SR volume. On re-annotated MSD Task08 and HVM datasets, VascuSR outperforms interpolation and learning-based SR baselines in segmentation accuracy (Dice and clDice) and 3D vascular structure (connectivity and mean centerline distance), while maintaining image quality comparable to its SR backbone. Compared with learning-based baselines, VascuSR reduces class-averaged connected-component counts by over 20% on both datasets and mean centerline distance by over 10% on MSD.

nodes.title: Where Should the Gaussians Go? Reusable Label-Aware Allocation for Budget-Constrained Gaussian Splatting of Cinematic CT
nodes.authors: Bowen Xiang, Dingjie Su, Jon S. Heiselman, Michael I. Miga
nodes.summary: Anatomical labels help 3D Gaussian splatting preserve vessels in cinematic renderings of CT, but the representation is still found by optimising each patient's scene, where densification decides where Gaussians go, while real-time displays cap their number. We address one part of this process: deciding where a fixed budget of B Gaussians should be placed. We propose a reusable, labelaware allocation front end that maps a patient's CT, labels and transfer function to a density over 2mm cells and draws exactly B positions from it without per-patient optimisation; the other Gaussian attributes are still fitted per patient. The front end is learned once from per-patient optimised scenes and implemented as a population-trained neural prior and an interpretable seven-parameter visibility-aware closed form (VACF). With identical attribute fitting on 20 held-out patients at 10K-100K Gaussians, both raise vessel-masked PSNR over uniform allocation by 4.5-7.1dB and over pruning a dense voxel-aligned model by 1.6-3.3dB. The neural prior does not differ significantly from per-patient optimised allocation at any budget, and VACF is within 0.6dB of it on vessels; on 19 external patients the neural prior again matches it on vessels and VACF is within 0.7dB. As an initialisation for position optimisation, VACF allocation beats per-patient densification on vessels at 10K Gaussians and, at 25K, reaches a higher vessel PSNR after 118s of optimisation than densification after 248s. Under altered rendering presets, VACF transfers to new colours and lighting but not to a label-free transfer function, whereas the neural prior shows the opposite pattern.

nodes.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
nodes.authors: Yongzhen Hu, Hao Yu, Jiawei Wang, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu, Xingliang Liu, Ruizhen Hu, Xiaowei Zhou, Hujun Bao, Sida Peng
nodes.summary: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: Event Cameras versus Frame Cameras for Synthetic-Aperture Imaging: A Simulation Study
nodes.authors: Jakob Hinterholzer, Mohamed Youssef, Oliver Bimber
nodes.summary: Synthetic-aperture imaging (SAI) removes occluders such as foliage by integrating many views of a scene along a camera path. It has so far been used mainly with frame cameras. We ask whether an event camera has advantages for SAI, and answer the question in simulation, where both sensors see exactly the same scene and the same camera movement. A densely rendered Blender sequence is turned into frames with an EMVA~1288 noise model of an industrial global-shutter camera, and into an event stream with the v2e simulator parameterized like a Sony IMX636. The frames are integrated with the existing airborne optical sectioning renderer. For the events we add a new integration path that projects every single event onto the focal plane at its own interpolated pose, so no events have to be binned into frames. We compare the two sensors in three main runs and an additional dark high-speed test. In a bright scene at 25,m/s the frame camera records only three images on the path and cannot remove the occluder, while the event camera reconstructs the target, even after an event-rate controller drops most of its events to fit the camera link. At the same speed in a 5,lux scene the event camera no longer resolves the target either. In a 5,lux scene at 5,m/s both sensors reconstruct the target at similar quality. We also compare the data one traversal of the aperture costs. At high speed the capped event stream still shows the target at the same data volume as the three frames. At 1,m/s we compare both cameras at two matched data budgets, and there the event camera has no advantage over the frame camera in reconstruction quality. The data rate of the event camera depends on the scene and is highest exactly in the fast bright scenes where it is needed most.

nodes.title: GLoD-LVSM: Learning Geometry-Grounded Continuous-LoD Scene Representations for Large View Synthesis Models
nodes.authors: Weikai Lin, Nicholas Milef, Carl S Marshall, Grant Kaijuin Yang, Todd Keeler, Yuhao Zhu
nodes.summary: Large view synthesis models (LVSMs) reconstruct scenes from sparse views and render novel views quickly, but they incur unnecessary storage and rendering costs due to token redundancy. We present GLoD-LVSM, a compact, geometry-grounded scene representation for LVSMs with continuous levels of detail. First, instead of learning a fixed set of scene anchor initializations, GLoD-LVSM learns a continuous field that initializes a flexible number of anchors to match the desired budget. A condenser then aggregates scene information into these anchors, with both the field and condenser trained end-to-end. Second, the condenser infers reference-token and anchor geometry to guide compression through geometry-grounded attention, improving rendering quality and enabling frustum culling during decoding. Compared with existing LVSM scene-compression baselines, GLoD-LVSM achieves the best trade-off between rendering quality and scene token count. Compared with the uncompressed base model, GLoD-LVSM reduces the scene-token count by 33.4% and accelerates rendering by $1.23\times$ with no quality loss. Under a relaxed quality-loss budget, the reduction increases to 85.5%, with $3.00\times$ rendering speedup. Further analysis reveals that view-synthesis supervision yields emergent scene depth and self-organized anchors that align with surfaces and adapt their density to local texture complexity. Beyond rendering, we further show that our scene representation also supports scene-semantic understanding, highlighting its potential for broader downstream tasks.

nodes.title: Contrastive uncertainty learning for robust multi-structure segmentation in lower-pelvic MR
nodes.authors: Bilal Sidiqi, Yipei Wang, Wen Yan, Shaheer U. Saeed, Daniel C. Alexander, Yipeng Hu
nodes.summary: Boundary delineation of anatomical structures in prostate MRI is often compromised by regional ambiguity. Automated segmentation methods relying on global overlap loss functions tend to be insensitive to surface deviations, leading to significant errors in ambiguous regions. Most existing uncertainty-aware methods treat uncertainty as a post-hoc quality indicator or prediction filter. We propose Contrastive Uncertainty Learning (CUL), a supervised framework that uses predictive uncertainty to directly guide representation learning. Using Monte Carlo Dropout, CUL identifies voxel-wise uncertainty and structures the embedding geometry accordingly: low-uncertainty, correctly predicted features form stable voxels while high-uncertainty or misclassified features are actively repelled, preventing feature collapse at difficult boundaries. We evaluate CUL on a 589-scan 3D prostate MRI multi-structure segmentation task (8 anatomical structures) using a ViT with UperNet decoder architecture. Average Dice ($83.38\%$) remains comparable to the baseline ($83.35\%$), while surface distance decreases significantly ($p<0.001$) across 6 of 8 anatomical structures. A hard-case analysis reveals a $22{\times}$ asymmetry between significantly improved and degraded cases ($18.8\%$ vs $0.9\%$). Ablation studies show that removing uncertainty-guided sample selection eliminates improvements for the transition zone, while replacing the contrastive objective with a boundary loss additionally removes bladder improvements, demonstrating that both uncertainty-guided sampling and the contrastive objective are essential for the observed gains. These findings demonstrate that the proposed uncertainty-guided representation learning is a useful mechanism for reducing the risk of extreme errors in safety-critical medical segmentation
